in_hebrew.name: מנואלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מנואלה היא שם תאופורי שמקורו בעברית, המשמר את הרעיון של נשמה של אלוהים. השם נזכר בקרב יהודים ונוצרים, כמייצג את הקשר בין האל והבשר. בדוגמת יהושע, נשמתו של האל הייתה חייה, השם מנואלה יכול לסמל את השלמות האלוהית המושגת בעולם הבשר.

in_greek.name: Μανουέλα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μανουέλα είναι μια ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος Μανουήλ, που προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό Μנואל. Ο Μανουήλ ήταν ο ονόματος του πατέρα της Μαρίας, της μητέρας του Ιησού. Η ονομασία Μανουέλα συνδέεται επίσης με την ιδέα της ψυχής του Θεού, που ζούσε μέσα στην ανθρώπινη φύση.

in_latin.name: Manuela
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Manuela est forma Latina nominis Manuæl, quod ex Hebraico Manu'el derivatur. Manuæl erat nomen patris Mariæ, Matris Jesu. Nomen Manuela itaque est conectum cum idea animæ Dei, quæ in naturâ humana habitavit.

in_english.name: Manuela
in_english.meaning: daughter of God, soul of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Manuela is a feminine form of Manuel, which originates from the Hebrew name Manu'el. Manu'el was the name of the father of Mary, the mother of Jesus. The name Manuela is connected to the idea of the soul of God, which dwelled in human nature. This concept is rooted in the Christian tradition, where the divine and human natures of Jesus are seen as inseparable. The name Manuela thus symbolizes the union of the divine and human, reflecting the Christian understanding of the Incarnation.

biblical_reference.note: The name Manuela is connected to the biblical figure of the angel Gabriel, who announced the birth of Jesus to Mary.

data.cultural_impact: The name Manuela carries a rich and significant cultural heritage that can be traced back to the Latin origins of the name. The word ‘manus’ itself refers to the hand, a powerful symbol of healing, creation, and service in various cultures and religions. In the Portuguese-speaking world, the name Manuela is popular and widely used. Historically, this name was given to girls born into families who saw the hand of God in their lives. It is a reminder of the divine intervention and protection that the Saint Manuela provided through her miraculous healings throughout her life and after her death.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Manuela stems from its connection to the Latin phrase ‘manus Dei’. In Christianity, this phrase is deeply meaningful, as it symbolizes the presence and providence of God with His people. Manuela is not just a name; it is a reminder of the promise and commitment of God to be with His children in every moment of their lives. Throughout her life, Saint Manuela embodied the virtues of faith, compassion, and Servant leadership. Her powerful relationship with God enabled her to provide healing and comfort to the people around her. Today, the name Manuela can serve as an inspiration and reminder of God's love and always being present with us.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Manuela was a popular name among the Visigoths in the 5th century. The name Manuela carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
